penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Any 'managed Proxmox vGPU configuration service' requires hands-on system access and per-customer technical work; even a guide product needs significant expert curation per GPU model and driver version combination.

rationale: The pain is real — operators with $10k+ GPU cards want to maximize utilization — but the buyer is poorly defined (DevOps engineers at small AI labs are a heterogeneous, hard-to-reach audience who skew toward solving problems themselves via forums rather than paying for guides), and there is almost no willingness-to-pay signal for this type of niche infrastructure documentation. Lead reachability is weak: this audience lives on Reddit, ServerFault, and Discord but is resistant to paid products for configuration help. Operational autonomy is moderate at best for a static guide, but any service component collapses it. The deciding factor is that after the human fulfillment penalty, total drops to 2.7 — well below the validate threshold — and the audience size for 'Proxmox + L40s vGPU' is extremely small.
solution_plan: This is not a viable standalone micro-service for a solo non-technical operator. The closest viable version would be a highly specific technical guide (PDF or web page) on configuring mixed vGPU profiles on Proxmox with Nvidia L40s, sold for $29-79 on Gumroad. However: the audience is tiny and self-sufficient (they debug on forums for free), willingness to pay for documentation is low, and producing an accurate, trustworthy guide requires genuine hands-on Proxmox/Nvidia expertise the factory cannot fabricate. If the operator has direct experience with this stack, a Gumroad guide could be worth a small experiment, but it is unlikely to generate meaningful revenue. Recommend dropping.
notes: Fails buyer_clarity build_gate (score 4, floor 6), willingness_to_pay build_gate (score 4, floor 5), operational_autonomy build_gate (score 5, floor 7), and buildability_with_ai build_gate (score 5, floor 6). Total after penalties (2.7) is far below min_total_to_validate (5.5). Drop. Signal strength of 2 from a single low-engagement forum post reinforces this.
